finding: The authors combine a pretrained seq2seq generator with neural retrieval over a dense Wikipedia index, comparing sequence-level and token-level passage conditioning. Their abstract reports more specific, diverse and factual generated language than a parametric-only seq2seq baseline.
method: Abstract describes fine-tuning and evaluation on knowledge-intensive NLP tasks, including three open-domain QA tasks and language generation.
limitations: Abstract only: no factuality effect size, uncertainty interval, evaluation rubric, sample size or ablation details. QA performance is not a direct hallucination-rate estimate.

finding: The authors study retrieval, ranking and encoder-decoder architectures for knowledge-grounded dialogue. The abstract reports state-of-the-art performance on two conversational tasks and substantial reduction in knowledge hallucination according to human evaluations.
method: Architectural comparisons on two knowledge-grounded conversational tasks and human evaluation, as described in the abstract.
limitations: Abstract only: no numerical hallucination reduction, human-evaluation protocol, annotator agreement, sample size or uncertainty estimates. Component-specific contributions cannot be isolated from the abstract.
